howGpsWorks.modalTitle: How GPS Finds You — 7-Step Interactive Guide
howGpsWorks.modalSubtitle: Discover how satellites 20,200 km in space pinpoint a receiver in Yerevan with nanosecond precision

step1.title: Satellite Broadcasts Navigation Signal
step1.description: Each satellite carries ultra-precise atomic clocks (Rubidium / Cesium) accurate to 1 nanosecond. The satellite continuously broadcasts its orbital coordinates (ephemeris) and the exact nanosecond transmission timestamp $t_{tx}$ via radio frequency carrier waves (L1: 1575.42 MHz).

step2.title: Signal Travels Toward Earth
step2.description: Radio photons traverse outer space vacuum at the speed of light ($c \approx 299,792\text{ km/s}$). As the signal descends through Earth's ionosphere and troposphere, electron density and atmospheric water vapor slightly refract and delay the signal path.

step3.title: Receiver Measures Signal Timing
step3.description: The receiver's antenna picks up the faint electromagnetic signal (approx -160 dBW). The receiver's internal quartz oscillator records the local reception timestamp $t_{rx}$, calculating total signal transit time $\Delta t = t_{rx} - t_{tx}$ (typically ~67 to 85 milliseconds).

step4.title: Receiver Estimates Pseudorange
step4.description: Multiplying transit time by light velocity yields the raw distance: $\rho = c \cdot \Delta t$. It is called a 'pseudorange' because the receiver's quartz clock is not perfectly synchronized with the satellite's atomic clocks, introducing a clock bias offset $b$.

step5.title: Multiple Satellites Provide Ranging Spheres
step5.description: 1 satellite puts the receiver on the surface of a giant sphere. 2 satellites narrow the position to the circular intersection of 2 spheres. 3 satellites narrow it to two points on Earth. At least 4 satellites are mathematically required to simultaneously solve for 3D coordinates $(X, Y, Z)$ and the receiver clock bias.

step6.title: Receiver Calculates 3D Position & Clock Offset
step6.description: The receiver's digital signal processor runs a non-linear least-squares or Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) solving a system of 4 simultaneous equations: $\rho_i = \sqrt{(x_i - X)^2 + (y_i - Y)^2 + (z_i - Z)^2} + c \cdot \Delta t_{bias}$. This instantly solves user $(X, Y, Z)$ and eliminates local clock error!

step7.title: Accurate Position Appears on Your Map
step7.description: Earth-Centered Earth-Fixed (ECEF) coordinates are mapped to WGS-84 ellipsoidal latitude, longitude, and height. The exact coordinate pin — whether in Yerevan, Armenia or anywhere on the globe — appears with sub-5-meter precision!

dop.title: Dilution of Precision (DOP)
dop.explainer: DOP measures the multiplier effect of satellite geometry on positioning errors. Satellites spread widely across the sky yield optimal (low) DOP values.
